Rain taps gently on the windowpane—a soft percussion against the glass. I love this sound. Not the furious drumming of a storm, but this quiet, persistent rhythm that turns the world outside into a watercolor blur. It’s a permission slip to slow down, to linger over a cup of tea that’s too hot to sip, to watch the steam curl like ghostly ribbons into the air.  

There’s a forgotten book on the armchair—spine cracked, pages slightly yellowed. I pick it up, breathe in the scent of old paper and dust, and remember reading it years ago, under different skies, with a younger heart. Stories are time machines. They hold echoes of who we were when we first met them.  

Outside, a sparrow flits between branches, shaking off droplets like tiny diamonds. Life persists, even in the hush. I think about how much we miss when we’re always rushing—how beauty hides in the ordinary: in the way light slants through a dusty room, in the quiet hum of a refrigerator, in the space between heartbeats.  

Maybe peace isn’t something we find far away on mountaintops or beaches. Maybe it’s right here, in the stillness between raindrops, in the courage to sit with ourselves without distraction. In this moment, I am nowhere and everywhere at once—anchored in my chair, yet floating through memory and imagination.  

The rain continues. And for now, that’s enough.
